Date : 22.03.2023 Heard Mr. I. Hussain, learned counsel for the petitioner.

Also heard Mr. P.
Borthakur, learned Additional Public Prosecutor for the State respondent.

This is an application under Sections 397/401 read with Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973, praying for setting aside and quashing the impugned order dated 20.02.2023,
passed by the learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate (M), Bijni, whereby, the learned Court below rejected the zimma petition filed by the petitioner in connection with Bijni P.S. Case No.

Om Prakash Singh vs The State Of Assam And Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is submitted by the learned counsel for the petitioner, Mr. I. Hussain, that the learned Court below has passed the order only with a view that the power under Section 451 Cr.P.C. can be exercised only during enquiry or trial and the order was passed based on the judgment and order passed by this Court in Crl. Pet. No. 597/2022, dated 16.09.2022.

It is further submitted that the petitioner is a registered owner of the seized vehicle and the vehicle is no way connected with the seized areca nuts and the vehicle is a private one for his own use.

Further it is submitted that the vehicle is in the custody of the police for last 2 (two) months, but the learned Court below did not consider all these facts and rejected the petition for zimma only considering the fact that the case is at the stage of investigation.

In this context, the learned Additional Public Prosecutor, Mr. P. Borthakur, has submitted that the earlier zimma petition was rejected by the learned Court below observing that Section 451 Cr.P.C. cannot be exercised during the investigation.

The learned Court below also made an observation of difference between the investigation and the enquiry as defined under Section 2(g)
Cr.P.C.

Accordingly, it is submitted that the petitioner can move a fresh application before the learned Court below under Section 457 Cr.P.C. and that can be entertained by the learned Court below making an enquiry regarding the ownership of the present vehicle.

Considering the submissions of learned counsels of both sides and also considering the view expressed by a larger Bench of this Court, passed in Crl. Pet./284/2022, dated 02.03.2023, the petitioner is hereby directed to file fresh petition for zimma before the learned Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Bijni District, Chirang, and after ascertaining the ownership of the vehicle and considering the stage of investigation etc., the learned Court below shall, accordingly, dispose of the matter in accordance with law.
With the above observation and direction, this criminal revision petition stands disposed of.
